navAboutBody: MarginLab is a decision studio that reads your portfolio as a collateral engine. It shows the cost, risk, and whether your portfolio can carry a trade before you open it.

footerDisclaimer: MarginLab — an educational simulator. Not real investment advice.
pageGeneralTitle: Combine portfolio, margin and scenario logic into a single decision flow.
pageGeneralTitle2: Portfolio, margin and scenarios on one canvas.
pageGeneralDesc: Explain first — then calculate. MarginLab reads your portfolio as a collateral engine; it shows the cost, risk and resilience of a trade before you open it.
pageGeneralGuidedBody: Use the Guide (book) icon top-left to toggle these notes. Each page shows you the decision first, then the logic.
heroTitle: How healthy is your portfolio right now?
heroBody: Of its total value {total}, {invested} is in stocks and {cash} is in cash. Your largest position weighs {concentration}.
costMicro: Total cost is the minimum return threshold needed to be profitable. On a small portfolio this can reach 3-5%.
profileGeneralDesc: A general educational model. Eligible securities count toward account-level collateral at an assumed 75%.
profileCashFirstDesc: A conservative model. Securities produce no collateral; only cash counts as available collateral.
profileConservativeDesc: Securities count toward collateral but at a lower effective rate (~2/3 of nominal). Shows haircut sensitivity.
marginDisclaimer: Calculated with the selected account profile and collateral assumptions. Actual broker rates, eligibility and liquidation conditions may differ.
scenarioBullDesc: Strong uptrend. Market and trade gain value together.
scenarioHypeDesc: Excessive optimism. Trade gets an inflated premium, portfolio only rises slightly.
scenarioPeakDesc: Peak exhaustion ~ S&P correction June 2022. Trade hard, portfolio medium shock.
scenarioSlowBleedDesc: Slow bleed. Long-term gradual erosion, 1% drop per day.
scenarioCreditStressDesc: Silent killer. Current portfolio loses value, trade stays flat.
scenarioTechSelloffDesc: Tech selloff ~ NASDAQ correction Q4 2022. Hits a tech-heavy portfolio.
scenarioRecoveryDesc: Recovery. Market turns up again after the shock.
scenarioFlatDesc: Price stays flat. Only the carry cost (interest) silently accrues — this is the profit threshold.
conceptInitialBody: The minimum equity ratio you must put in from your own pocket when opening a position on margin. Under SEC Reg T it is generally 50%; so for $1,000 of stock you put at least $500 and the rest is broker credit. Formula: Required Equity = Position Value × Initial Margin.
conceptInitialExample: The "Initial margin %" slider in the simulator sets this rate. Required equity at open is calculated from here.
conceptMaintenanceBody: The minimum equity ratio that must be maintained in the account while a position is open. FINRA standard is 25% for long positions; most brokers apply a 25-30% "house" rule. When equity drops below this, a margin call triggers.
conceptMaintenanceExample: At 25% maintenance: a margin call starts the moment Equity < Market Value × 0.25.
conceptCallpriceBody: The stock price at which the position breaks the maintenance threshold. Formula: Call Price = Debt / (Shares × (1 − Maintenance)). If price falls below this, you are called: either add cash or sell part of the position.
conceptCallpriceExample: The simulator's right panel shows the call price and the distance (buffer) to the current price.
conceptBufferBody: The percentage distance between the current price and the margin call price. A positive buffer means you are safe until prices drop that much. Zero buffer = called at today's price. Negative = already in trouble.
conceptBufferExample: The "Margin Buffer" KPI on the dashboard and the warning box in the simulator change color by buffer state.
conceptCollateralBody: The contribution of your holdings to your margin capacity. Brokers count not the full value of a stock but a certain ratio (haircut); e.g. 75%. Total available collateral = Cash + ∑(Stock Value × Collateral Rate).
conceptCollateralExample: In the Portfolio tab you can adjust each stock's collateral rate; this directly affects whether you can open a new trade.
conceptConcentrationBody: When a single position or sector is overweight in the portfolio. Brokers apply extra haircuts to concentrated positions. The product shows this clearly in the health score and the finder's sector penalty.
conceptConcentrationExample: If a stock is over 40% of your portfolio, a red "Concentrated" badge lights up.
conceptCarryBody: The interest on the margin debt; it accrues silently every day. It erodes the position even if price is flat. Most visible in the Flat scenario.
conceptCarryExample: The "Annual margin interest" slider in the simulator shows this cost.
conceptScenarioBody: Tests the same trade across nine different market environments. Each scenario shows how margin amplifies both gains and losses.
conceptScenarioExample: The Flat scenario is the most instructive: price never changes but carry cost still produces a loss.
conceptBuffer2Body: The distance between the current price and the margin call threshold; if positive you are above the maintenance threshold.
conceptBuffer2Example: The Finder's "worst-case" mode surfaces the one that stays standing even in bad markets.
warnNeutralNote: Produces no collateral in this profile
warnRationaleNote: If account-level collateral falls below the maintenance requirement a margin deficiency may arise; extra cash/collateral can be added or the position reduced. If the shortfall persists, positions may be reduced/liquidated per account terms, and the order in which positions are sold may not always be under your control. Forced liquidation behavior depends on the actual account and broker terms.
simDesc: What if I buy this trade on margin? See portfolio collateral and scenario drawdown in real time.
simGuidedBody: The call price on the right panel is where you break the maintenance threshold. Buffer is the distance from the current price to that threshold: if positive you are above the maintenance threshold, if zero you are called today.
simCollSecNone: Produces no collateral in this profile
simCollMarketDep: Share of pool tied to market price
simCollRiskNote: In this simulation collateral is evaluated at account level; no specific stock is allocated to this trade. If the value of eligible holdings in the portfolio drops, collateral capacity also drops.
simCostMicro: Total cost is the minimum return threshold needed to be profitable.
simPostMicro: This is the account-level margin state with the trade added to the current portfolio. The PDT rule (max 2× leverage under $25,000 accounts) is checked automatically.
simProjectionMicro: Daily drop {drop} · {days} days. The red dot is the first day the margin call appears. The dashed line is how interest/carry erodes equity while price is flat — it silently wears away even on a flat price.
assumStatic: Data is sample/static — not live market data.
assumSource: Price source: marketData.json (sample universe), current price is fixed.
assumCollateral: Collateral rate: default 75%, may be user input or broker rule.
assumScenarios: Selected scenarios: "{active}" active; result may not depend on a single scenario.
assumBroker: To verify with broker: call price, collateral rate and current interest terms.
settingsWatchlistNote: Watchlist stocks appear as a separate group in the simulator, scenario and finder pickers even if not in your portfolio.
portDesc: The collateral engine of your positions. Each stock produces available buying power for a new trade.
portGuidedBody: The Collateral % on each row determines how much of that stock's value counts toward your margin capacity. Brokers discount less liquid/hamil stocks (haircut). The safe default is 75%.
portEmptyBody: You can load the sample portfolio to start or import your own JSON. All data stays in your browser, nothing is sent anywhere.
portAdvNote: Cash and eligible positions form a single account-level collateral pool; the system evaluates all of them automatically.
portAdvNoteOn: The counted rate is how much of the stock's value counts as credit collateral (post-haircut credit value — not the stock value). The default assumed value is %{rate}.
portAdvNoteOff: Enable Advanced Assumptions to edit rates, exclude positions and simulate haircuts.
portConcDetail: {ticker} makes up %{pct} of your portfolio. This demo model does not auto-reduce the collateral rate; under real broker terms the collateral value could be lower.
portLowCashDetail: Your cash ratio is below 10%; a small drop could create a forced collateral requirement.
portHaircutSim: Simulate {ticker}'s collateral rate as %{from} → %{to} due to concentration? This is only a simulation assumption.
scenDesc: Test the same trade across eight different market environments. Margin amplifies both gains and losses.
scenGuidedBody: The Flat scenario is the most instructive: price never changes but the carry cost (interest) still produces a loss. This is the silent cost of margin.
scenResilienceNote: You stay above the maintenance threshold in {controlled} of {total} scenarios.
scenStressDesc: Below is the account-level margin state of the entire current portfolio under the selected scenario's daily drawdown.
scenEarlyWarningSub: The day you break the {pct}% buffer threshold
scenFlatNote: Price is flat but carry cost produces a loss — the silent cost of margin.
scenFragileNote: In this scenario the account drops below the maintenance threshold; a margin call triggers.
scenWatchNote: Buffer is thin; a small additional drop breaks the threshold.
scenSafeNote: In this scenario the structure stays above the maintenance threshold.
findDesc: Find the trade that yields the best result for this budget and portfolio. Each card explains why it stands out.
findGuidedBody: In Worst-case mode #1 is the trade that stays standing even in bad scenarios. In Selected-only mode #1 is only the best for the current scenario. They differ.

eduDesc: Why does margin logic work this way? Follow these five steps before using the decision support tools.
eduGuidedBody: This page teaches concepts in order. The concept link in each step shows the term's counterpart in the product.
eduStep1Body: Each of your holdings is at the same time a collateral line. The value of CSCO, CSWC, TRIN and GFS produces buying power for a new trade. Cash is the purest collateral.
eduStep1Task: Find the holding with the largest weight in your portfolio.
eduStep2Body: Margin is the credit you take from the broker. Its interest accrues daily. If you fall below maintenance margin you are called: add cash or sell.
eduStep2Task: Check the maintenance margin rate (FINRA standard 25%).
eduStep3Body: Initial margin (Reg T 50%) is the equity you must put in at open. In the simulator you can adjust this rate and the maintenance rate yourself.
eduStep3Task: Enter a trade in the simulator and watch the call price.
eduStep4Body: Test nine scenarios instead of a single price. In the Credit Stress scenario the current portfolio drops while the trade stays flat — the silent killer.
eduStep4Task: Find the early-warning day and interest layer in the Peak scenario.
eduStep5Body: The Finder ranks the most resilient trade for your budget and portfolio. The worst-case mode surfaces the one that stays standing even in bad markets.
eduStep5Task: Try the worst-case mode in the Finder and read the resilience badge.
eduWarnThinBufferBody: If buffer is below 10% a small drop pushes you to the margin call threshold. Reduce the lot or raise the collateral rate.
eduWarnConcBody: If a stock is over 40% of your portfolio the broker applies extra haircut; diversification is lost.
eduWarnRateBody: Carry cost is silent: even if price is flat, debt interest erodes the position. See this in the Flat scenario.
eduWarnMobileBody: Actions on top, numbers tabular-aligned. The key decision comes first, detail a tap away.
eduWarnIconBody: No icon is used alone; every visual has meaning beside it. Accessibility is a priority.
alertNakitAz: Cash is under 5% of your portfolio. The room to act without selling for a margin call is almost nonexistent.
alertNakitDusuk: Your cash ratio is below 10%. A small drop could create a forced collateral requirement.
alertHealthBalanced: Health {health}/100 — a balanced and resilient structure.
finderRationaleConc: {sector} sector already at %{pct} weight — increasing concentration
alertAsiriConcBody: A single position is over 40% of your portfolio. The broker may apply a collateral discount (haircut) and diversification is lost.
alertConcTakipBody: Your largest position weighs over 30%. Review sector diversification.
alertYuksekDuyarliBody: Weighted beta is above 1.6; the portfolio erodes faster than average in market downturns.
alertYapiSaglamBody: Your cash, concentration and beta values are balanced. You can use margin while keeping this structure.
profileSelDisclaimer: This is not a broker integration; collateral rates are mock/assumed.
mcmSubtitle: New trade + current portfolio together; scenario/shock matrix
mcmMicro: Each day: trade + portfolio value, collateral, accrued interest and maintenance threshold are calculated together. Threshold 0 = margin call; dashed line = early-warning (buffer %{ewPct}).
mcmSelectCell: Select a cell — account summary, which threshold is exceeded and corrective actions are shown.
simNoMarket: No market data — enter price manually

settingsGlobalNote: These are global defaults; the active profile can override them with its own values.

portDesc: Positions are the collateral engine. Each share produces usable buying power for new trades.
portCollateralGuideBody: The Collateral % on each row sets how much of that share's value counts toward your margin capacity. Brokers apply discounts (haircuts) to less liquid/pledgeable shares. The safe default is 75%.

portAdvEditBody: The counted rate is how much of the share's value is treated as credit collateral (post-haircut credit value — not the share value). The default assumed value is {rate}%. Changing this rate, excluding a position, and the haircut simulation are each simulation-only assumptions; real margin accounts apply collateral and liquidation decisions at account level and do not guarantee any asset is ring-fenced for a specific trade.

conceptCollateralBody2: Collateral is the asset base that backs opening a new trade. It is automatically composed of cash and eligible portfolio positions; the active account profile and data source set the rates.
conceptInitialBody2: Initial margin is the equity requirement the account must meet to open a trade. In the active account profile it can be satisfied with cash plus eligible portfolio collateral.
eduStep3Body2: Initial margin is the equity requirement the account must meet to open a trade. In the active account profile it can be satisfied with cash plus eligible portfolio collateral. In the simulator you can adjust this rate and the maintenance rate yourself.
recommendedActionMc: Position is in the margin-call zone — add cash or collateral, or reduce the position.
recommendedActionMr: Very close to the maintenance threshold — a small drop would trigger a call.
recommendedActionEw: Buffer is thin — be cautious about further downside.
recommendedActionControlled: Structure stays above the maintenance threshold.
